paper_title: First Axion-Like Particle Results from a Broadband Search for Wave-Like Dark Matter in the 44 to 52 $μ$eV Range with a Coaxial Dish Antenna
suggested_experiment_name: GigaBREAD (Broadband Reflector Experiment for Axion Detection)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: First axion-like particle search with a dish antenna. Exclusion limit extracted from Figure 3 at the 90% confidence level in the 44–52 μeV (10.7–12.5 GHz) mass range. The limit is approximately flat across this range at ~2.8×10^-12 GeV^-1. No signal observed above 3σ threshold. DM density of 0.45 GeV/cm³ is the standard halo density used in the signal power formula (Eq. 2). The experiment used a 3.9 T solenoid magnet at Argonne National Laboratory with a coaxial horn antenna. Total systematic uncertainty is 21% (Table I). The blind injected test signal at 11.68 GHz was successfully recovered, validating the analysis procedure. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.92, 58)) | Vision: Panel (a) of FIG. 3 shows the GigaBREAD exclusion limit (green shaded region) on axion-like particle photon coupling in the 44–52 μeV mass range. The y-axis label explicitly shows '×10^-11' multiplier applied to the tick values [3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 5.5, 6.0], giving absolute coupling values in units of 10^-11 GeV^-1. The x-axis is in μeV (linear scale, 44–54 μeV). Converted to eV: 44 μeV = 4.4×10^-5 eV, 54 μeV = 5.4×10^-5 eV. The boundary shows a gentle upward slope consistent with the CAST constraint visible in the same panel. Dark matter density ρ₀ = 0.45 GeV/cm³ is noted on the plot. This is the first axion-like particle search using a dish antenna geometry, representing a novel experimental approach to probe the high-mass axion parameter space. | Calibration: No calibration needed
